newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh PM urges more local loans to entrepreneurs.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh PM urges more local loans to entrepreneurs.

text.p: Kazakhstan's reformist Prime Minister Akezhan Kazhegeldin on Wednesday welcomed a sharp fall in domestic Treasury bill yields and urged local banks to make more long-term loans to entrepreneurs.

"It is great that yields have fallen. This was our dream," Kazhegeldin told reporters. He added that instead of relying on income from state securities, "...it is high time (for banks) to start lending money to small hair-dressing salons, shops or small tourist companies."

Local banks have said one of the major reasons for steeply falling T-bill yields was aggressive buying by foreigners, who are entitled to buy 15 percent of each issue of three-month paper and 30 percent of six- and 12-month bills.

The yield on Kazakh three-month MKM discount T-bills fell to 12.29 percent annual at an auction on Tuesday from 14.59 percent at the last auction on May 20. Six-month T-bills yielded 16.24 percent on Monday, compared to 19.90 percent on May 12.
The banks have complained that the government is pushing them into making new long-term loans to the private sector, while there is still an overhang of overdue debts.

But the National Bank has said government securities are still paying a good return, and falling yields reflect the outlook for inflation this year, which could fall below the official target of 17 percent.

Kazhegeldin said, "Bankers complain because now they face a lot of discomfort -- they face higher risks, they now have to work personally with every client, so that he opens an account at their banks and does not flee (to another banks)."

The premier said that the government understood the bankers' concerns about overdue loan payments and added that the legislature was about to start discussions on a draft law providing for tough punishment of defaulters.
